accuracy.reason: Separates time, space, and source age without refresh or freshness promises.

evidence.quote: TTL limits an entry's lifetime, not the age of the source data used to fill it.

mechanisms.reason: Expiry leads to a later reader's load, while capacity removal can happen earlier.

evidence.quote: Sets how long an entry may remain before it expires. A 60-second TTL does not refresh the product every minute; a later miss must load it again.

coherence.reason: Connects removal to previously taught misses and fills, preserving source ownership.

evidence.quote: A product can be evicted before its TTL ends. Some configurations reject new entries when full instead of evicting existing ones.

decisions.reason: Sufficient distinctions to reason about retention and capacity behavior, though TTL duration tradeoffs are not developed here.

evidence.quote: Removes entries to make room. A least-recently-used policy favors removing entries that have not been read recently.

clarity.reason: TTL and eviction have compact definitions with an explicit everyday timing example.

outcomes.reason: Correct stale 09:02 hit, 09:06 expiry miss, 09:04 eviction miss, time versus capacity distinction, no freshness/retention guarantee, and application-driven later replacement; all entailed by prefix.
